title: Yod Hebrew Letter (י): Sound & Words
description: Learn the Hebrew letter Yod (י), also spelled Yud: its [y] sound, how it helps spell the vowel [i], words like יָד (hand), plus interactive practice.

blocks.0: Yod Hebrew Letter (י): Sound, Words & Practice
blocks.2: Yud has a small written form and can work in two ways. As a consonant, it represents [y], as in יָד [yad]. It can also help spell a vowel. For example, in בִּי [bi], the dot under Bet (Hiriq) and the following Yud represent [i], like ee in English 'see'; there is no separate [y] sound. In both practice words below, Yud is pronounced as a consonant.
blocks.5: The word יָד [yad] means 'hand' or 'arm' and has one syllable. It consists of Yud (י) and Dalet (ד). Kamatz Gadol under Yud (יָ) represents [a], giving [ya]. Dalet at the end of the word adds [d]. Read the sounds together: [yad].
blocks.7: The adjective חַי [chay] means 'alive' or 'living' in the masculine singular. It has one syllable. Chet (ח) gives the sound written ch in this course, as in German 'Bach' or Scottish 'loch'. Patah under Chet (חַ) adds [a]. Yud at the end of the word adds the [y] glide: read ay smoothly, like English 'eye', to make [chay].

4.tip: Yud can also help spell a vowel. In בִּי [bi], the dot under Bet (Hiriq) and the following Yud represent [i], with no separate [y].

15.tip: Patah represents [a]. With Chet, חַ is read [cha]; Yud at the end of the word completes חַי [chay].

theory.heading: Meet Yod
theory.intro: The tenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet. Yod, also spelled Yud (the spelling used in this lesson), is one of the smallest Hebrew letters, and it does two jobs: as a consonant it makes a [y] sound, as in “yes,” and it can also help spell the vowel [i]. It looks like a short Vav (ו) that stops halfway, hanging near the top of the line.
objectives: Hear its consonant [y] sound, as in “yes.”
Read Yod in real words like <bdi class="hebrew" lang="he" dir="rtl">יָד</bdi> (hand), and notice when it helps spell a vowel.

examples.heading: Yod in real words
examples.intro: See Yod in two new Hebrew words, and review the Kamatz Gadol and Patah vowel marks from earlier letters.
